07-01.s: Hungarian physician Ignaz Semmelweis, who discovered the cause of puerperal (childbed) fever and introduced handwashing antisepsis into maternity care, was born in Buda.
German physician Karl von Vierordt was born; he later developed techniques and instruments, including early sphygmographic tools, for monitoring blood circulation.

07-02.t: Jonas Salk Conducts First Human Polio Vaccine Trial
07-02.s: Virologist Jonas Salk and staff at the D.T. Watson Home for Crippled Children in Sewickley, Pennsylvania, injected 43 children with his experimental killed-virus polio vaccine.

07-03.s: American physician Valentine Seaman, who introduced the smallpox vaccine to the United States and mapped yellow fever outbreaks in New York City, passed away.

07-04.s: American surgeon John Murray Carnochan, credited with performing the first successful neurosurgical procedure for trigeminal neuralgia, was born in Savannah, Georgia.
Physician and pharmaceutical pioneer Edward Robinson Squibb was born in Wilmington, Delaware, later establishing high-purity ether production and founding E. R. Squibb & Sons.

07-05.s: French surgeon Mathieu Jaboulay was born; he made some of the earliest attempts at kidney transplantation in humans with chronic kidney failure using animal grafts.
American-British bacteriologist George Nuttall was born; he investigated the relationship between mosquito distribution and malaria transmission.

07-06.s: Louis Pasteur and physician Jacques-Joseph Grancher began administering the first human attenuated rabies vaccine to nine-year-old Joseph Meister after he was mauled by a rabid dog.
Swedish biochemist Hugo Theorell was born; he later won the Nobel Prize for elucidating the nature and action of oxidation enzymes, including alcohol dehydrogenase.

07-07.s: Italian physician and pathologist Camillo Golgi was born; he developed the silver staining technique for nervous tissue and identified the Golgi apparatus.
Russian neuroscientist Natalia Bekhtereva was born; she authored more than 360 works, including studies on the biopotentials of cerebral hemispheres in human brain tumors.

07-08.s: French military surgeon Dominique Jean Larrey was born; serving Napoleon's Grande Armée, he pioneered battlefield triage and mobile ambulance units.
French psychologist Alfred Binet was born; he co-created the Binet-Simon scale, the first practical intelligence test.

07-09.s: American physician Charles Caldwell, who founded what became the University of Louisville School of Medicine, died in Louisville, Kentucky.

07-09.t: Daniel Hale Williams Performs First Successful Open-Heart Surgery
07-09.s: At Provident Hospital in Chicago, surgeon Daniel Hale Williams successfully repaired a stab wound to the pericardium of patient James Cornish without X-rays or antibiotics.

07-10.s: American medical physicist Edith Quimby, a founder of nuclear medicine who advanced diagnostic and therapeutic X-ray dosing and radiation safety, was born.

07-11.s: Japanese molecular biologist and 1987 Nobel laureate Susumu Tonegawa, who discovered V(D)J recombination explaining antibody diversity, passed away in San Mateo, California.

07-12.s: Japanese microbiologist Satoshi Ōmura was born; he discovered Streptomyces avermitilis, leading to avermectin and ivermectin, earning him a share of the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
American pediatrician and geneticist Gregg L. Semenza was born; he discovered HIF-1 and shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for how cells sense and adapt to oxygen.

07-13.s: British pharmacologist Joshua Harold Burn, a pioneer in applying statistical methods to pharmacology and bioassays of vitamins and hormones, died in Oxford.

07-14.s: German physiologist and comparative anatomist Johannes Peter Müller was born; his work advanced understanding of voice, speech, hearing, and sensory physiology.
English nurse, physician, and founder of the modern hospice movement Cicely Saunders, who transformed palliative care for terminally ill patients, passed away.

07-15.s: American virologist and epidemiologist Thomas Francis Jr. was born; he isolated influenza A and B viruses, developed polyvalent flu vaccines, and directed the 1954 Salk polio vaccine field trials.
Immunologist Élie Metchnikoff, who discovered phagocytosis and cell-mediated immunity and won the 1908 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, died in Paris.

07-16.s: American epidemiologist Joseph Goldberger was born; working for the U.S. Public Health Service, he proved that pellagra is caused by dietary deficiency rather than infection.

07-17.s: Brazilian physician and pharmacologist Sérgio Henrique Ferreira, who discovered bradykinin potentiating factor and paved the way for ACE inhibitor antihypertensive drugs, passed away.

07-18.s: American psychiatrist Aaron T. Beck was born; he pioneered cognitive therapy and developed the Beck Depression Inventory (BDI) and Beck Anxiety Inventory (BAI).
American psychiatrist Karl Menninger, co-founder of the Menninger Foundation and Menninger Clinic, passed away.

07-19.s: American surgeon Charles Horace Mayo was born; he co-founded the Mayo Clinic and specialized in thyroid and nervous system surgery.

07-19.t: NIH HuBMAP Releases Multi-Organ Human Cell Atlases
07-19.s: Scientists from the NIH Human BioMolecular Atlas Program published detailed cellular maps of the human kidney, intestine, and placenta showing gene and protein activity.

07-20.s: Moravian-Silesian scientist Gregor Mendel, founder of modern genetics who established the fundamental laws of heredity, was born.
Polish-born chemist Tadeusz Reichstein was born; he synthesized vitamin C in 1933 and later shared the 1950 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for adrenal cortex hormones.

07-21.s: French chemist and physicist Henri Victor Regnault was born; he designed sensitive thermometers and calorimeters foundational to physiological measurement.

07-22.s: Polish-Jewish pediatrician, educator, and children's advocate Janusz Korczak was born; he directed a children's orphanage and championed pediatric welfare.
Biochemist and microbiologist Selman Waksman was born; he discovered over twenty antibiotics, including streptomycin, and coined the modern medical term 'antibiotic'.

07-23.s: Australian pathologist Robin Warren, who co-discovered Helicobacter pylori and proved peptic ulcers are an infectious bacterial disease, died in Perth.

07-24.s: Biochemist Fritz Lipmann, who discovered coenzyme A and shared the 1953 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for elucidating cellular energy metabolism, passed away.

07-25.t: Birth of Louise Brown, First IVF Baby
07-25.s: Louise Joy Brown was born in England as the world's first baby conceived via in vitro fertilization (IVF), following pioneering work by Patrick Steptoe and Robert Edwards.

07-26.s: French dermatologist Philippe Gaucher was born; he first described Gaucher's disease, a lysosomal storage disorder, and founded Annales des Maladies Vénériennes.
Swiss psychiatrist and psychotherapist Carl Jung, founder of analytical psychology, was born.

07-27.s: Puerto Rican physician and sociologist José Celso Barbosa was born; he initiated an early form of employer-funded health insurance.

07-27.t: Banting Team Proves Insulin Regulates Blood Sugar
07-27.s: Led by Frederick Banting, researchers at the University of Toronto demonstrated that the pancreatic hormone insulin regulates blood glucose levels.

07-28.s: American physician and geneticist Baruch Samuel Blumberg was born; he identified the hepatitis B virus, developed its diagnostic test and vaccine, and won the 1976 Nobel Prize.
Swedish ophthalmologist Allvar Gullstrand, who won the 1911 Nobel Prize for his work on the dioptrics of the eye and invented the reflex-free ophthalmoscope, died in Stockholm.

07-29.s: German-born Israeli gynecologist Bernhard Zondek was born; he developed the first reliable pregnancy test in 1928.
American physicist Isidor Isaac Rabi was born; he won the 1944 Nobel Prize for discovering nuclear magnetic resonance, the physical basis of MRI.

07-30.s: Dutch physician Reinier de Graaf was born; he discovered the ovarian follicles (Graafian follicles) and coined the term 'ovary' for the female mammalian gonad.
American physician Jonathan Mann was born; he served as a WHO administrator and spearheaded global AIDS research and public health response in the 1980s.

07-31.s: American physician and public health official Leroy Edgar Burney, who served as the eighth Surgeon General of the United States from 1956 to 1961, passed away.
American gynecological surgeon and IVF pioneer Howard W. Jones Jr., who co-founded the clinic behind the first U.S. IVF birth and treated Henrietta Lacks in 1951, died at age 104.
